facts.value: Few laws protect student's social media privacy. Organizations such as the ACLU call for more privacy protection. They urge students who are pressured to give up their account information to resist.
facts.programme_association: Social and Cultural Analysis (Women and Gender Studies) - BA

facts.value: Colleges and universities may access applicants' internet services including social media profiles as part of their admissions process.
facts.programme_association: Social and Cultural Analysis (Women and Gender Studies) - BA

facts.value: In 2012, 27% of admissions officers used Google to learn more about an applicant, with 26% checking Facebook.
facts.programme_association: Social and Cultural Analysis (Women and Gender Studies) - BA

facts.value: Students whose social media pages include questionable material may be disqualified from admission processes.
facts.programme_association: Social and Cultural Analysis (Women and Gender Studies) - BA

facts.value: A survey in July 2017 reported that 11 percent of respondents said they had refused to admit an applicant based on social media content.
facts.programme_association: Social and Cultural Analysis (Women and Gender Studies) - BA

facts.value: This includes 8 percent of public institutions, where the First Amendment applies.
facts.programme_association: Social and Cultural Analysis (Women and Gender Studies) - BA

facts.value: 30 percent of institutions acknowledged reviewing the personal social media accounts of applicants at least some of the time.
